name: Kovas Kaunas
content:
ŠŠ Kovas Kaunas was a Lithuanian football club based in Kaunas and is considered one of the strongest teams of the country’s interwar period. The club was founded in 1921 as a local branch of a physical education organization in the Šančiai district and was renamed “Kovas” in 1923. From its early years, the team quickly established itself as a major force in Lithuanian football.

During the 1920s and 1930s, Kovas achieved significant success in the Lithuanian championship, winning six national titles and finishing as runners-up multiple times. The club also competed internationally against teams from countries such as Austria, Hungary, and Estonia, reflecting its strong level and reputation. In addition to football, the organization supported other sports, including basketball, ice hockey, boxing, and table tennis, making it a multi-sport club.

The club’s existence came to an end during World War II and the Soviet occupation of Lithuania. Around 1944–1945, Kovas was dissolved and later reorganized into another team under the Soviet system. Despite its disappearance, the club remains an important part of Lithuanian football history due to its achievements and influence during the early development of the sport in the country.

name: KSS Klaipėda
content:
KSS Klaipėda was a Lithuanian football club founded in 1926 in the city of Klaipėda. It represented the Klaipėda region during the interwar period and quickly became the strongest football team in the city. The club was originally part of a broader sports organization and played an important role in promoting Lithuanian football in a region with a diverse cultural and political background.

During the late 1920s and 1930s, KSS Klaipėda was one of the leading clubs in Lithuania. It won six national championship titles and regularly competed at the top level of the Lithuanian football championship. The team also achieved several runner-up finishes and maintained a strong reputation, even playing international matches against foreign opponents, which reflected its high competitive standard at the time.

The club’s history was heavily influenced by political events in the region. In 1939, following a German ultimatum, Klaipėda was annexed by Nazi Germany, forcing the team to relocate to Telšiai and temporarily change its name. Shortly afterward, in 1940, the club was dissolved amid the broader geopolitical changes of World War II, bringing an end to one of Lithuania’s most successful interwar football teams.

name: LFLS Kaunas
content:
LFLS Kaunas was one of the earliest and most influential football clubs in Lithuania, founded in 1919 in Kaunas. The team represented the Lithuanian Physical Education Union and played a key role in introducing and developing football in the country. It was a multicultural club in its early years, bringing together players of different nationalities, which reflected the diverse environment of interwar Lithuania.

The club was a pioneer of Lithuanian football infrastructure and organization. It established the first football field and stadium in Kaunas, launched the country’s first sports newspaper, and helped create the national football league in 1924. On the field, LFLS was highly successful, winning several Lithuanian championships, including the first two titles in 1922 and 1923, and remaining one of the strongest teams during the interwar period.

LFLS Kaunas continued competing until World War II, but its activities were disrupted by political changes and Soviet occupation. The club was dissolved around 1945, marking the end of its historic era. Although it was briefly revived in the late 1990s, it did not achieve lasting success, but it remains an important part of Lithuanian football history due to its pioneering role and early achievements.

name: LFLS Kaunas 2
content:
LFLS Kaunas “dubleriai” (reserve team) were the second squad of LFLS Kaunas, one of the strongest Lithuanian football clubs during the interwar period. In the early years of Lithuanian football, reserve teams were sometimes allowed to compete in the same national championship structure, and LFLS II became a rare example of such a case. The team was formed to develop younger players and provide depth for the main squad.

The reserve side made a surprising impact in the very first Lithuanian championship season in 1922. Despite being a second team, LFLS Kaunas II managed to compete at the highest level and achieved an unexpected success by finishing in third place in the national league. This result made them the only known reserve team in interwar Lithuanian football to reach the podium in the top division.

After the 1922 season, the structure of Lithuanian football became more organized, and reserve teams were no longer part of the main championship in the same way. As a result, LFLS II disappeared from top-level competition. However, their achievement in 1922 remains a unique historical fact, highlighting the early and experimental nature of Lithuanian football development.

name: LGSF Kaunas
content:
LGSF Kaunas was a Lithuanian football club based in Kaunas and one of the most prominent teams during the interwar period. The organization behind the club, the Lithuanian Gymnastics and Sports Federation, was founded in 1922 by Karolis Dineika and Juozas Eretas. It was a large multi-sport association with dozens of sections and strong ties to Christian democratic movements, promoting physical education and sports across Lithuania.

The football team itself was established in 1927 and quickly rose through the ranks of Lithuanian football. Within a year, it was promoted to the top division and became a regular competitor at the highest level. LGSF Kaunas also played international matches against clubs from countries such as Estonia, Poland, and the Netherlands, reflecting its growing strength and reputation in the region.

The club achieved its greatest success in the late 1930s, winning the Lithuanian championship in the 1938–39 season and finishing as runners-up and third-place contenders in several other years. Its activities came to an end in 1944 due to the political and military upheavals of World War II. Despite its relatively short existence, LGSF Kaunas remains an important part of early Lithuanian football history.

name: Maistas Kaunas
content:
Maistas Kaunas was a Lithuanian football club based in Kaunas, founded in 1932 and associated with the “Maistas” food industry company. It was one of the early examples of a company-backed football team in Lithuania, reflecting the growing connection between industry and sport during the interwar period. The club quickly became competitive and was among the participants in the top-level Lithuanian championship during the 1930s.

The club achieved its greatest success in 1934 when it won the Lithuanian national championship, marking its place among the strongest teams of that era. During the 1930s, FK Maistas Kaunas remained active in top-tier competitions and contributed to the development of football in the country, alongside other notable clubs from Kaunas.

Its activities were interrupted during World War II, and the club disappeared around 1941 due to the geopolitical upheavals in the region. It was later re-established after Lithuania regained independence in 1990, but mainly competed in lower divisions and never regained its former status. The club ultimately dissolved in 1995, ending its long but intermittent history in Lithuanian football.

name: Tauras Kaunas
content:
FK Tauras Kaunas was a Lithuanian football club based in Kaunas, founded in 1928 during the interwar period. Initially, the team was established as a branch of LFLS Kaunas, one of the leading football organizations in the country at the time. Over the following years, Tauras developed into an independent club and became part of the Lithuanian championship system.

The club gradually progressed through the league structure and reached the top division after the 1934 season. During the late 1930s and early 1940s, Tauras Kaunas competed regularly at the highest level and achieved its greatest success by winning the Lithuanian championship in the 1942–43 season. This victory marked the peak of the club’s sporting achievements during its relatively short history.

Like many Lithuanian clubs of that era, Tauras Kaunas was heavily affected by World War II and political changes in the region. In 1944, following the Soviet reoccupation of Lithuania, the club was dissolved and ceased to exist. Despite its disappearance, Tauras Kaunas remains a notable part of Lithuanian football history as one of the competitive teams of the interwar and wartime periods.

name: FK Pagėgiai
content:
FK Pagėgiai is a Lithuanian football club from the town of Pagėgiai, located in the western part of the country. The club has had a long and fragmented history, with its origins going back to the interwar period when a team called Sportverein Pagėgiai represented the local community in regional competitions. During that time, the club competed in the Klaipėda zone of Lithuanian football championships in the mid-1920s.

After the interwar period, football activity in Pagėgiai went through several reorganizations and name changes, especially during the Soviet era and after Lithuania restored independence. The club was known under different names such as Melioratorius, Rembutas, and Ąžuolas before eventually becoming FK Pagėgiai again. It mainly competed in lower regional leagues and served as a community-based team rather than a top-tier club.

In the modern era, FK Pagėgiai continues to participate in lower divisions of Lithuanian football, including amateur and regional competitions. It has also been linked at times with larger regional clubs, acting as a feeder or satellite team. Although it has never achieved major national success, the club remains an important part of local football culture in Pagėgiai and the surrounding region.

name: MSK Panevėžys
content:
MSK Panevėžys was a Lithuanian football club based in Panevėžys that originated in the interwar period. The team was initially founded in 1935 under the name Maisto sporto klubas (MSK), representing workers connected to the local food industry. It quickly became part of the national football system and participated in Lithuanian championships during the late 1930s and 1940s.

During the wartime and post-war years, MSK Panevėžys remained one of the key football representatives of the city. The club reached notable success in the early 1940s, finishing as runner-up in national competitions, although many seasons were disrupted or unfinished due to World War II and political instability. After the Soviet occupation, the team continued to exist in various forms and still represented Panevėžys in regional and republic-level competitions.

In the Soviet period, the club underwent several reorganizations and name changes, reflecting changes in sponsorship and local industry. It eventually became part of a larger sports structure in the city, later known under different names, before its identity was absorbed into other local teams. Despite this, MSK Panevėžys remains an important part of the early football history of the city and is considered a predecessor of later Panevėžys football clubs.

name: FK Kuršiai
content:
FK Kuršiai was a Lithuanian football club from Klaipėda. It was founded in 1936 and represented one of the local sports organizations in the coastal city during the interwar period. The club’s name “Kuršiai” refers to the Curonian people and the historical Curonian Lagoon region, reflecting its strong regional identity and connection to Klaipėda’s cultural heritage.

During its active years, FK Kuršiai participated in regional competitions and the early structure of Lithuanian football championships. The club competed mainly against other Klaipėda-based and regional teams, contributing to the development of organized football in western Lithuania. While it was not among the dominant clubs in the country, it played an important role in maintaining a competitive football scene in the region.

Like many interwar Lithuanian clubs, FK Kuršiai was affected by the political changes and disruptions of World War II. The club eventually disappeared as organized football in the region was interrupted by occupation and wartime instability. Despite its short and limited history, FK Kuršiai remains part of the early football heritage of Klaipėda and Lithuania’s interwar sporting landscape.

name: LFLS Vilnius
content:
LFLS Vilnius was a Lithuanian football club based in the capital city, formed as part of the broader Lithuanian Physical Education Union (LFLS) sports movement. The LFLS system was one of the most important early organizers of sport in interwar Lithuania, and Vilnius had its own branch that helped promote football locally. The club represented the same tradition as LFLS Kaunas and other LFLS teams across the country, focusing on developing structured football and physical education.

During the interwar period, LFLS clubs, including the Vilnius branch, were among the strongest football participants in Lithuania. These teams regularly competed in national championships and helped establish early football standards in the country. LFLS Vilnius players also contributed to the broader Lithuanian football scene, with many players involved in national-level competitions and inter-club matches that shaped early football development.

Like most Lithuanian sports organizations of the era, LFLS Vilnius was heavily affected by World War II and the subsequent Soviet occupation. The disruption of independent Lithuanian sports structures led to the disappearance or reorganization of many LFLS clubs. Although the Vilnius branch did not survive as an independent team in the long term, it remains part of the historic LFLS network that played a key role in building Lithuanian football in its early decades.

name: FK Žalgiris
content:
FK Žalgiris is a Lithuanian professional football club based in Vilnius and one of the most successful teams in the country’s history. Founded in 1947 as Dinamo Vilnius, the club later adopted the name Žalgiris, referencing the historic Battle of Žalgiris (Grunwald). It has long been a symbol of Lithuanian football, producing many notable players and representing the country in both domestic and international competitions.

During the Soviet era, Žalgiris competed in the USSR league system and became one of the strongest teams from the Baltic region. The club gained particular recognition in the 1980s when it reached the top tier of Soviet football and developed a strong fan base. After Lithuania regained independence in 1990, Žalgiris became a dominant force in the national league, winning multiple championships and establishing itself as the leading club in modern Lithuanian football.

In recent years, FK Žalgiris has continued its success domestically and achieved historic milestones in European competitions. In 2022, the club became the first Lithuanian team to reach the group stage of a UEFA club tournament, marking a significant achievement for the country’s football. With numerous league titles, national cups, and a strong supporter culture, Žalgiris remains a central figure in Lithuanian football.

name: FBK Kaunas
content:
FBK Kaunas was a Lithuanian football club based in Kaunas and one of the most successful teams in the country’s modern era. The club’s origins date back to 1960, when it was founded as Banga Kaunas, and it later evolved into FBK Kaunas in the early 1990s after Lithuania regained independence. The club’s name reflected its connection to both football and baseball, as it operated as a multi-sport organization.

The club reached its peak between the late 1990s and late 2000s, becoming the dominant force in Lithuanian football. FBK Kaunas won eight A Lyga titles, including six consecutive championships from 1999 to 2004, as well as multiple Lithuanian Cups and Super Cups. It also achieved international recognition, most notably winning the Baltic League in 2008 and defeating Rangers in UEFA Champions League qualification, marking one of the most famous results in Lithuanian club football history.

However, the club declined rapidly after 2008 due to financial and administrative issues, including the withdrawal of support from its main owner. It dropped to lower divisions and struggled to maintain stability before being dissolved in 2012. Despite its collapse, FBK Kaunas remains one of the most important and successful clubs in Lithuanian football history, particularly for its dominance during the early years of independence.

name: FK Ekranas
content:
FK Ekranas was a Lithuanian football club based in Panevėžys, founded in 1964. It originated as a team linked to a local electronics factory and became one of the main representatives of the city in football. During the Soviet period, the club competed in regional competitions and achieved notable success by winning the Lithuanian SSR championship in 1985.

After Lithuania regained independence in 1990, Ekranas became one of the leading clubs in the national league. It was among the founders of the A Lyga and enjoyed its greatest success in the 2000s and early 2010s, winning multiple league titles, including a dominant period with consecutive championships from 2008 to 2012. The club also won several Lithuanian Cups and Super Cups, establishing itself as one of the most successful teams in modern Lithuanian football.

Despite its success, the club faced serious financial problems in the mid-2010s. After the 2014 season, it failed to meet licensing requirements and was declared bankrupt, leading to its dissolution in 2015. A new club, FK Panevėžys, was later formed to represent the city, while FK Ekranas was eventually re-established in 2020 and now competes in lower divisions.

name: FK Sūduva
content:
FK Sūduva is a Lithuanian professional football club based in Marijampolė, founded in 1942. It is one of the main teams representing the Suvalkija region and has been a regular participant in Lithuania’s top division. The club’s colors are traditionally white and red, and it plays its home matches at the Marijampolė Arena, a modern stadium built in 2008.

During the Soviet era, Sūduva competed in regional Lithuanian SSR competitions, generally achieving moderate results. After Lithuania regained independence in 1990, the club became part of the new national football system but initially struggled, even experiencing relegation in the early years. Its fortunes improved in the 2000s, and since 2002 the team has been a consistent member of the top league, gradually becoming more competitive.

The club reached its peak in the late 2010s, winning its first Lithuanian championship in 2017 and successfully defending the title in 2018 and 2019. Sūduva also won several domestic cups and super cups, establishing itself as one of the strongest Lithuanian teams of the modern era. It has also participated regularly in European competitions, further strengthening its reputation in Baltic football.

name: FK Kareda Kaunas
content:
FK Kareda Kaunas was a Lithuanian football club that originated in Šiauliai and later relocated to Kaunas. The club was originally founded in 1990 as Sakalas Šiauliai and went through several name changes before becoming FK Kareda in 1996. It competed in Lithuania’s top division during the 1990s and quickly rose to prominence with strong financial backing and ambitious management.

The club reached its peak in the late 1990s, becoming one of the strongest teams in Lithuanian football. FK Kareda won back-to-back A Lyga championships in 1997 and 1998 and also secured multiple Lithuanian Cup victories. During this period, it attracted some of the best players in the country and even participated in European competitions, marking its status as a leading club of that era.

However, the club’s success was short-lived due to financial and organizational problems. After losing its main sponsorship in 1999, Kareda was sold and moved to Kaunas in 2000, where it became closely linked to FBK Kaunas. Due to ownership restrictions, it could not continue competing at the same level and gradually declined before being dissolved in 2003. Despite its brief existence, FK Kareda remains notable for its rapid rise and success in Lithuanian football during the late 1990s.

name: FK Inkaras Kaunas
content:
FK Inkaras Kaunas was a Lithuanian football club based in Kaunas, founded in 1937 and closely linked to the “Inkaras” rubber factory. The club was part of a broader industrial sports tradition, where factory teams played a major role in developing football in Lithuania. From its early years, Inkaras became one of the key teams representing Kaunas in national competitions.

During the Soviet period, the club achieved significant success, winning multiple Lithuanian SSR championships, particularly in the 1950s and 1960s. It was also one of the few Lithuanian teams that occasionally participated in the wider Soviet football system beyond the republic-level competitions. Inkaras additionally enjoyed success in domestic cup competitions, collecting several Lithuanian Cup titles and building a reputation as a strong and consistent team.

After Lithuania regained independence, FK Inkaras remained competitive and reached its peak in the mid-1990s, winning back-to-back A Lyga titles in 1995 and 1996 and also securing the Lithuanian Cup and Supercup. However, the club declined in the following years due to financial and organizational issues and eventually withdrew from competitions in 2003. Despite its dissolution, Inkaras is remembered as one of the historically successful clubs in Lithuanian football.

name: FK Kauno Žalgiris
content:
FK Kauno Žalgiris is a professional football club based in Kaunas, Lithuania, competing in the country’s top division. It was originally founded in 2004 as FM Spyris Kaunas and later became part of the wider Žalgiris sports organization. In 2016, the club adopted its current name, aligning itself with the famous Žalgiris brand and strengthening its identity within Lithuanian sport.

The club entered the top tier of Lithuanian football in 2015 and gradually established itself as a competitive side. Although it struggled in its early seasons, often finishing in lower positions, it improved steadily over time. By the late 2010s and early 2020s, Kauno Žalgiris became a regular contender for top positions, achieving podium finishes and qualifying for European competitions.

Its greatest success came in 2025, when the club won its first Lithuanian championship, marking a historic achievement. The team also secured the Lithuanian Supercup in 2026 and has continued to represent Lithuania in European tournaments. Today, Kauno Žalgiris is considered one of the leading modern clubs in Lithuanian football, reflecting steady growth and development since its founding.

name: FK Sirijus Klaipėda
content:
FK Sirijus Klaipėda was a Lithuanian football club based in Klaipėda, founded in 1973. The team was originally linked to a local industrial enterprise and initially competed under a slightly different name before adopting “Sirijus” in 1989. It played its home matches at the Žalgiris Stadium and became one of the notable football clubs in the city during the late Soviet and early independence periods.

The club achieved its greatest success around the end of the 1980s and the beginning of the 1990s. It won the Lithuanian Cup twice, in 1988 and 1990, and became the first champion of independent Lithuania in 1990 after the collapse of the Soviet system. Sirijus was also one of the founding members of the A Lyga and remained competitive in the early years of the national league.

In the following years, the club’s performance declined, and it struggled to maintain its earlier success. By the mid-1990s, financial and organizational problems led to its dissolution, and in 1996 the team was absorbed into another Klaipėda club, FK Atlantas. Despite its relatively short existence, FK Sirijus Klaipėda is remembered as an important team in Lithuanian football history, particularly for its role in the first years of independence.

name: ROMAR Mažeikiai
content:
ROMAR Mažeikiai was a Lithuanian football club based in the city of Mažeikiai, founded in 1992 during the early years of Lithuania’s restored independence. The club was created by businessman Romas Marcinkevičius, whose investment allowed it to take over the place of an existing local team in the top division. From the beginning, ROMAR quickly became a competitive side in the A Lyga, benefiting from strong financial backing and player recruitment.

The club achieved remarkable success in a very short time. After finishing sixth in its debut season, ROMAR Mažeikiai won the Lithuanian championship in the 1993–94 season, becoming one of the strongest teams in the country. It followed this achievement with a third-place finish in 1994–95, confirming its status as a top-level club during that brief period.

Despite its rapid rise, the club’s success was short-lived. When its main sponsor left Lithuania, financial support collapsed, and the team was unable to continue operating at a high level. ROMAR Mažeikiai was dissolved in 1995, after only a few years of existence, and was later replaced by a successor club in the city.

name: FK Panevėžys
content:
FK Panevėžys is a Lithuanian professional football club based in the city of Panevėžys. It was founded in 2015 after the financial collapse and dissolution of the city’s previous top club, FK Ekranas. The new club was created to restore top-level football in the region and began its journey in the second tier of Lithuanian football before quickly rising to the A Lyga, the country’s top division.

In its early years, the club steadily developed both sportingly and structurally. After gaining promotion to the A Lyga in 2018, FK Panevėžys established itself as a stable top-flight team. It gradually improved its league positions and also began achieving success in domestic cup competitions, including winning the Lithuanian Football Cup in 2020, which marked its first major trophy.

The club reached its historic peak in the early 2020s. FK Panevėžys won the Lithuanian championship for the first time in 2023, becoming one of the top teams in the country. It also earned opportunities to compete in UEFA competitions, representing Lithuania in European tournaments. Today, the club is considered a strong and modern force in Lithuanian football, continuing the football tradition of Panevėžys after the era of FK Ekranas.

name: FC Hegelmann
content:
FC Hegelmann is a Lithuanian professional football club based in Raudondvaris, in the Kaunas district. It was founded in 2009 as FC Hegelmann Litauen by the German logistics company Hegelmann Group. The club’s name comes from the founding Hegelmann family, and it was originally created as a lower-division team with the long-term goal of reaching professional football in Lithuania.

The club started in the lower tiers of Lithuanian football and gradually climbed through the system. After winning promotion from the II Lyga in 2018, it continued its rise and reached the I Lyga, where it finished second in 2020, earning promotion to the A Lyga, Lithuania’s top division. In its debut top-flight season in 2021, Hegelmann immediately established itself as a competitive mid-table side.

In recent years, FC Hegelmann has become one of the strongest modern clubs in Lithuanian football. It has consistently finished near the top of the A Lyga, including runner-up positions in 2024 and 2025, and has also reached Lithuanian Cup finals. The club now regularly competes in European qualification tournaments and is considered a stable and ambitious force in the country’s top division.

name: FA Šiauliai
content:
FA Šiauliai is a Lithuanian football club based in the city of Šiauliai. It was founded in 2007 as the Football Academy of Šiauliai after the merger of local youth sports structures. The club was initially created as a development-focused academy, aiming to train young players, but over time it grew into a fully professional organization with senior men’s, women’s, and youth teams.

The men’s team gradually climbed through the Lithuanian football pyramid, starting from lower regional divisions and progressing step by step to higher leagues. After competing in II and I Lyga, the club earned promotion to the A Lyga in 2021, marking its debut in the top tier of Lithuanian football. Since then, FA Šiauliai has established itself as a stable mid-table team and has also participated in domestic cup competitions and European qualifiers.

In the modern era, FA Šiauliai is considered an important development club in Lithuania, known for combining youth training with competitive senior football. The club continues to build its reputation in the A Lyga, consistently finishing in the upper half of the table and occasionally competing for European qualification spots. Its structure also includes reserve and women’s teams, making it one of the more comprehensive football academies in the country.

name: FK Riteriai
content:
FK Riteriai is a Lithuanian professional football club based in Vilnius. It was founded in 2005 under the name FK Trakai and originally functioned as a community-based project aimed at promoting youth football and physical activity. The club started in the lower tiers of Lithuanian football and gradually climbed through the league system through steady sporting development.

After progressing through the divisions, Riteriai reached the A Lyga, Lithuania’s top division, in 2014. In its early top-flight years, the club quickly established itself as a competitive side, achieving strong results and finishing near the top of the league, including runner-up positions in 2015 and 2016. During this period, it also reached domestic cup finals and regularly participated in European qualification rounds.

In 2019, the club moved from Trakai to Vilnius and adopted the name FK Riteriai, meaning “The Knights.” Since then, it has remained a consistent participant in Lithuania’s top division, though with more mixed sporting results compared to its peak years. The club continues to operate a youth academy and focuses on player development while competing in national and occasional European competitions.

name: FK Atlantas
content:
FK Atlantas was a football club from Klaipėda, Lithuania, and one of the historically important teams in the country’s football development. It originated in 1962 under the name Granitas Klaipėda and later became Atlantas in the 1970s, reflecting the city’s strong maritime identity. During the Soviet period, the club competed in the Lithuanian SSR championship and was among the most successful regional teams, winning several titles at that level.

After Lithuania regained independence, FK Atlantas became a regular participant in the national A Lyga and established itself as one of the key clubs from western Lithuania. The team won Lithuanian Cups in the early 2000s and also achieved high league finishes, including runner-up positions. It regularly competed in European qualifiers, representing Klaipėda in international club competitions.

In the 2010s, the club’s situation gradually declined due to financial instability and later serious administrative problems, including match-fixing scandals. In 2019, FK Atlantas was expelled from the A Lyga, fined, and relegated to lower divisions, and shortly afterwards the club effectively ceased to exist at professional level. name: FK Kruoja Pakruojis
content:
FK Kruoja Pakruojis was a Lithuanian football club from the town of Pakruojis, founded in 2001. The team was created as a local football project and gradually developed into a competitive side in Lithuanian football. The club played its home matches at the Pakruojis Stadium and wore yellow and blue colours, which became its main identity.

Kruoja rose through the Lithuanian football system and reached the A Lyga, the country’s top division, in 2009. Its participation at the highest level came after other clubs withdrew, giving it the opportunity to compete in elite football. Over the following seasons, the club established itself as a solid mid-table team and even achieved strong league results, including a runner-up finish in 2014.

Despite some sporting success, FK Kruoja faced serious problems in its final years. In 2015, the club withdrew from the A Lyga amid match-fixing allegations and financial difficulties, which led to its dissolution in 2016. After its collapse, football in the city continued through a successor club, but Kruoja itself remained a short-lived yet notable part of Lithuanian football history.

name: FK Vėtra
content:
FK Vėtra was a Lithuanian football club based in Vilnius and originally founded in 1997 in the town of Rūdiškės. The club was created by businessman Romas Stašauskas and initially started in the lower divisions of Lithuanian football. After several years of rapid progress, it moved to Vilnius in 2004 and began playing in a newly developed stadium, becoming a regular participant in the country’s top football scene.

During the 2000s, Vėtra established itself as one of the stronger Lithuanian clubs outside the traditional giants. It consistently competed in the A Lyga, achieving several high league finishes, including a runner-up position in 2009 and multiple top-five results. The club also became known for its participation in European competitions, where it faced teams from Scotland, England, Poland, and other countries, gaining valuable international experience and some notable results.

Despite its sporting progress, FK Vėtra struggled financially in its final years. In 2010, the club was expelled from the Lithuanian top division due to serious financial difficulties and unpaid obligations, which led to its collapse and dissolution the same year. After its disappearance, the club’s infrastructure, including its stadium, was taken over and used by other Vilnius football organizations.

name: FK Panerys Vilnius
content:
FK Panerys Vilnius was a Lithuanian football club based in the capital city Vilnius. It was founded in 1975 and initially competed in lower tiers of Soviet Lithuanian football. The club’s name refers to the Paneriai region, a historical area of Vilnius located near the Neris River, which also influenced its identity and local support.

During the late Soviet period and the early years of Lithuanian independence, Panerys gradually reached higher levels of competition and became part of the national league system. In the early 1990s, the club competed in the top division and even achieved a runner-up finish in 1992, marking its strongest sporting period. However, it generally remained a mid-to-lower table team and struggled to establish long-term stability at the highest level.

In the late 1990s, the club faced serious decline. During the 1998–1999 season, Panerys withdrew from the A Lyga after only a few matches due to financial and organizational problems, and it was subsequently dissolved in 1998. Despite its short existence in top-level football, FK Panerys remains part of Vilnius football history as one of the clubs that participated in the early post-independence Lithuanian league system.

name: AFK Neris Vilnius
content:
AFK Neris Vilnius was a Lithuanian football club based in Vilnius. It was founded in 1966 and operated under several different names throughout its history, reflecting changes in sponsorship and organization. The club was part of the early development of Lithuanian football and later became one of the founding participants in the newly formed national league system after Lithuania regained independence.

During the early 1990s, Neris competed in the top division of Lithuanian football and even achieved strong results in its debut seasons. In 1991, the club finished as runner-up in the national championship, marking the peak of its sporting success. It also participated in early domestic cup competitions, where it managed to win a trophy in the 1991–92 season, making it one of the notable teams of the early independence period.

Despite its promising start, the club struggled with financial instability and organizational changes in the following years. Its performance declined during the mid-1990s, and by 1994 the club was dissolved and ceased to exist as an independent football team. Although short-lived, AFK Neris Vilnius remains remembered as one of the clubs that shaped the first years of modern Lithuanian football after independence.

name: FK Tauras Šiauliai
content:
FK Tauras Šiauliai was a Lithuanian football club based in Šiauliai, founded in 1971. The team was originally formed to represent the local “Tauras” television factory, which was common in Soviet-era sports structures where industrial enterprises supported football clubs. It quickly became one of the strongest teams in the city and established itself in regional Soviet Lithuanian competitions.

During the 1970s and 1980s, the club reached its sporting peak. FK Tauras Šiauliai won the Lithuanian SSR championship in 1974 and later finished as runners-up in 1980, marking its best results in the Soviet period. The team was coached for many years by Česlovas Urbonavičius and became one of the most recognizable clubs in Šiauliai football at that time.

After Lithuania regained independence, Tauras continued competing and even reached the Lithuanian Cup final in 1991, but soon struggled to maintain its top-level status. In 1992 the club was relegated from the highest division and played in lower leagues before eventually dissolving in 1994. Despite its disappearance, FK Tauras Šiauliai remains an important part of the city’s football history and is remembered as one of its strongest historical teams.

name: FK Banga Gargždai
content:
FK Banga Gargždai is a Lithuanian football club based in the town of Gargždai. It was founded in 1966 and originally functioned as a local sports team connected to an industrial enterprise. Over time, the club became an established part of Lithuanian football and developed a reputation as a stable regional team. It plays its home matches at the Gargždai Stadium and is known for its orange club colours.

Throughout its history, Banga has mostly moved between divisions, experiencing both promotions and relegations. The club competed in the top Lithuanian league during different periods, especially after 1990, and has often been a mid-table side in the A Lyga. One of its stronger eras came in the late 2000s and early 2010s when it secured a stable place in the top division after returning from lower leagues.

In recent years, FK Banga has grown into a competitive A Lyga team and achieved its best modern result by finishing fourth in the 2020 season. The club also won its first major trophy, the Lithuanian Cup, in 2024, marking the most successful achievement in its history. Today, Banga is considered a solid and ambitious provincial club in Lithuanian football, regularly competing at the top level and in European qualifiers.

name: FK TransINVEST
content:
FK TransINVEST is a very young Lithuanian football club based in Galinė, in the Vilnius district. It was founded in 2021 by the logistics company Transekspedicija as an ambitious project to build a professional team from scratch. The club quickly entered the Lithuanian football pyramid and began competing in the lower divisions with strong financial backing and rapid sporting development.

In its first seasons, TransINVEST experienced an extremely fast rise through the league system. After winning the II Lyga in 2022, the club immediately earned promotion and continued its success by winning the I Lyga in 2023. In the same year, it achieved a historic breakthrough by winning the Lithuanian Football Cup, becoming the first lower-division club to do so and earning a place in European competition.

In the following period, FK TransINVEST made its debut in the A Lyga and also participated in UEFA Conference League qualifiers. Although still a young club, it has already established itself as one of the most surprising success stories in modern Lithuanian football, known for its rapid progression and strong results shortly after its foundation.

name: FC Šiauliai
content:
FC Šiauliai was a Lithuanian football club based in the city of Šiauliai. It was founded in 2004 as a reorganization of earlier local football structures and became the city’s main representative in professional football. The club played its home matches at the Savivaldybė Stadium and competed in yellow and black colours, quickly establishing itself in the national football system.

After joining the A Lyga, FC Šiauliai spent more than a decade in Lithuania’s top division. The team generally performed as a mid-table side, with its best results coming in the early 2010s, when it achieved several strong league finishes and reached the Lithuanian Cup final in 2013. The club also represented Lithuania in European competitions, although without major success against stronger continental opponents.

Despite some sporting achievements, FC Šiauliai struggled with financial instability in its later years. The situation worsened by 2015, leading to unpaid wages and organizational difficulties. In 2016, the club was dissolved and ceased to exist as a professional team. Its legacy was later continued indirectly through the football academy system in Šiauliai, which became the foundation for new clubs in the city.

name: FC Stumbras
content:
FC Stumbras was a Lithuanian football club based in Kaunas, founded in 2013. It was created from the structure of the National Football Academy and quickly became one of the most ambitious modern projects in Lithuanian football. Starting from the lower divisions, the club achieved rapid success and climbed to the top tier within just a few seasons.

After entering the A Lyga in 2015, Stumbras established itself as a stable top-division team and gradually improved its performances. The club’s biggest achievement came in 2017, when it won the Lithuanian Football Cup, securing its first major trophy and earning qualification for European competition. In the following seasons, it also reached another cup final and finished as a strong mid-table side in the league.

Despite its sporting progress, FC Stumbras faced serious financial and organizational problems in 2019. The club lost its UEFA license, was expelled from the top division, and soon after ceased operations completely. Its dissolution marked a sudden end to one of the most rapidly rising clubs in Lithuanian football history, remembered for its short but successful existence.

name: FK Tauras Tauragė
content:
FK Tauras Tauragė is a Lithuanian football club based in the city of Tauragė, founded in 1942. It has a long history in Lithuanian football and has competed across different levels of the national league system. The club traditionally plays its home matches at Vytautas Stadium and is known for its red and black colours.

Throughout its history, Tauras has spent much of its time moving between divisions, but it has also had moments in the top tier of Lithuanian football. One of its most notable achievements came in the Soviet era when it won the Lithuanian SSR championship in 1987. In the modern period, the club has also had opportunities to compete in national cup competitions and occasional European qualifiers.

In recent years, FK Tauras has generally played in the lower professional divisions, focusing on rebuilding stability and maintaining its place in Lithuanian football. While it has not become a consistent top-flight contender, it remains an established club with a long tradition in Tauragė and continues to compete in national league structures.
